The San Diego Padres' 6-5 win over the San Francisco Giants produced the day's biggest WPA swing at 4.50 and tightened the NL West, as San Diego, Arizona, and Colorado all gained a game on the Dodgers, who fell to Boston. In the AL Central, Detroit picked up ground on the White Sox with a win over the Athletics.

  • Drew Rasmussen [6 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 2.92 ERA, PAR 39] led Tampa Bay past the White Sox 1-0, outdueling Chicago in a tight pitching battle. (TB)
  • Cristopher Sánchez [6 IP, 0 ER, 11 K | 2.62 ERA, PAR 54] and the Phillies shut out the Orioles 5-0 at Camden Yards. (PHI)
  • Hunter Goodman [4-5, 2 HR | RC 70] powered Colorado to a 12-6 win over Kansas City, with the Rockies gaining a game in the NL West. (COL)
  • Arizona outslugged Cleveland 12-8 behind Geraldo Perdomo [4-6, 1 HR | RC 50], gaining ground in the NL West. (AZ)
  • San Diego edged San Francisco 6-5 in the day's most dramatic finish, gaining a game on the Dodgers. (DODGERS)
  • Ceddanne Rafaela [2-4, 2 HR | RC 63] homered twice as Boston beat the Dodgers 3-2 at Dodger Stadium. (BOS)
  • Kevin McGonigle [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 70] and Framber Valdez [7 IP, 2 ER, 6 K | 4.42 ERA, PAR 23] led Detroit past the Athletics 8-6, gaining a game on the White Sox in the AL Central. (DET)
  • Martín Pérez [7 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 3.24 ERA, PAR 24] tossed seven shutout innings as Atlanta rolled past Washington 8-3. (ATL)

Both AL East and NL West leaders lost ground as their pursuers won across the board. The Rays fell to the White Sox while Baltimore, Boston, Toronto, and New York all won, and the Dodgers dropped a 9-4 decision to Boston as Arizona, Colorado, and San Diego all gained a game in the NL West.

  • The Reds edged the Pirates 8-7 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing, gaining ground in the NL wild card race. (PIRATES)
  • Yainer Diaz [4-5, 1 HR | RC 24] and Isaac Paredes [2-3, 2 BB, 1 HR | RC 57] powered the Astros to an 11-2 rout of the Rangers. (HOU)
  • Will Warren [6.2 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 4.16 ERA, PAR 23] tossed 6.2 shutout innings as the Yankees blanked the Cubs 2-0 at Wrigley. (NYY)
  • Dylan Cease [6 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 2.42 ERA, PAR 48] dominated in Toronto's 3-1 win over St. Louis, extending his AL strikeout lead. (TOR)
  • The Orioles beat the Phillies 6-4 and the Red Sox topped the Dodgers 9-4, both gaining in the AL East chase. (PHILLIES) (SOX)
  • The Tigers hammered the Athletics 13-1, gaining a game in the AL wild card race. (TIGERS)
  • Tomoyuki Sugano [6.2 IP, 1 ER, 2 K | 4.49 ERA, PAR 12] turned in 6.2 strong innings as the Rockies beat the Royals 3-1. (COL)
  • The Padres shut out the Giants 7-0 and the Marlins beat the Mets 5-2, with Miami gaining in the NL wild card race. (MARLINS) (GIANTS)

The White Sox knocked off the Yankees 2-1 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing, dropping New York another game back in the AL East while Tampa Bay's win over Texas kept the Rays comfortably atop the division. Meanwhile, the NL Central race tightened as both the Cubs and Reds gained half a game on the idle Brewers.

  • Sean Burke [6 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 3.05 ERA, PAR 39] and the White Sox stifled the Yankees in a 2-1 win, the day's biggest WPA swing. (CWS)
  • The Cubs beat the Cardinals 4-2 and the Reds edged the Pirates 3-2, each gaining 0.5 games on Milwaukee in the NL Central. (CUBS) (PIRATES)
  • Tampa Bay held off Texas 3-2, while the Angels and Astros both gained half a game on the Rangers in the AL West. (RANGERS)
  • Minnesota beat Kansas City 4-3, dropping the Royals a full game in the AL Central and boosting the Twins in the AL wild card race. (ROYALS)
  • Atlanta topped Washington 5-4 and the Mets beat Miami 4-2, sending both the Nationals and Marlins a game back in the NL East. (MARLINS) (NATIONALS)
  • Daylen Lile [2-4, 2 HR | RC 52] homered twice for Washington in a losing effort, posting the day's top LWTS mark. (WSH)
  • Noah Cameron [8 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 4.61 ERA, PAR 22] threw 8 shutout innings for Kansas City but got no decision as the Royals fell. (KC)
  • The Dodgers beat Seattle 6-2 and the Giants shut down San Diego 4-1, with Teoscar Hernández [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 34] and Robbie Ray [6 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 3.09 ERA, PAR 31] among the day's standouts. (LAD) (SF)

The Braves and Mets split a doubleheader at Citi Field, with Atlanta taking the nightcap 1-0 behind Chris Sale [6 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 2.08 ERA, PAR 48] to protect their NL East lead as Miami crept a half-game closer with a win over Philadelphia. The day's most dramatic finish came in Detroit, where the Orioles edged the Tigers 10-9 in a 5.24 WPA swing that cost Detroit ground in the AL Central.

  • Orioles def. Tigers 10-9 in the day's most dramatic game, dropping Detroit further back in the AL Central. (ORIOLES)
  • Braves and Mets split at Citi Field (NYM 3-2, ATL 1-0), with Chris Sale tossing 6 shutout innings in the nightcap. (ATL)
  • Marlins def. Phillies 8-6, gaining a half-game on Atlanta in the NL East as Philadelphia lost ground. (PHILLIES)
  • Cardinals def. Cubs 3-2 behind Matthew Boyd [7 IP, 0 ER, 5 K | 3.41 ERA, PAR 18]'s 7 scoreless innings, gaining a game on Milwaukee in the NL Central. (CHC)
  • Astros def. Angels 7-4 as Yainer Diaz [4-5, 1 HR | RC 21] went 4-for-5 with a homer, pulling Houston to within 1.0 GB of Texas in the AL West. (HOU)
  • Diamondbacks def. Pirates 3-0 behind Eduardo Rodriguez [8 IP, 0 ER, 2 K | 2.49 ERA, PAR 39]'s 8 shutout innings; Royals blanked Twins 4-0 as Randy Dobnak [7 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 1.04 ERA, PAR 10] went 7 scoreless. (AZ) (KC)
  • Giants routed Brewers 16-3 as Daniel Susac [2-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 14] hit two homers; Dodgers def. Mariners 4-2 with Eric Lauer [6 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 4.50 ERA, PAR 8] and Andy Pages [3-4, 1 HR | RC 63] leading the way. (SF) (LAD)
  • White Sox def. Yankees 6-5, Red Sox def. Athlet (YANKEES) (SOX)

The AL Central race tightened dramatically as first-place Chicago fell while all three chasers won: the Tigers hammered Baltimore 14-0, the Twins edged Kansas City, and the Guardians split a doubleheader in Cincinnati. Meanwhile, the Yankees pulled within 1.5 games of the AL East-leading Rays, and both Arizona and San Diego gained ground on the Dodgers, who fell to Seattle in a game featuring a 4.66 WPA swing.

  • Eduardo Valencia [4-5, 2 HR | RC 12] powered Detroit's 14-0 rout of Baltimore, the Tigers gaining a full game in the AL Central chase. (DET)
  • Cleveland and Cincinnati split a doubleheader 6-5 and 2-0, with Gavin Williams [7 IP, 2 ER, 12 K | 3.72 ERA, PAR 35] dominant on the mound in the opener. (CLE)
  • Arizona edged Pittsburgh 8-7 and San Diego outlasted Colorado 8-7, both NL West chasers gaining a game on Los Angeles; Fernando Tatís Jr. went a perfect 5-for-5 for the Padres. (SD)
  • Seattle beat the Dodgers 7-6 despite a big night from Shohei Ohtani [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR], with Dominic Canzone [2-4, 2 HR | RC 47] homering twice for the Mariners. (LAD)
  • Gerrit Cole [6 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 3.57 ERA, PAR 18] tossed six shutout innings as the Yankees beat the White Sox 3-2 to close within 1.5 games in the AL East. (NYY)
  • Sandy Alcántara threw seven scoreless in Miami's 1-0 win over Philadelphia, tightening the NL East as Washington also beat Toronto 8-6. (MIA)
  • The Cubs routed St. Louis 10-2, the Brewers handled the Giants 8-2, Houston edged the Angels 3-2, Texas beat Tampa Bay (CUBS) (ANGELS) (BREWERS)

The Mets battered the Braves 14-3 to cut Atlanta's NL East lead, with the Marlins also gaining a game on the leaders in a wild 8-7 win over Philadelphia. Meanwhile, the Cubs' 7-3 win at St. Louis pulled Chicago closer in the NL Central, while the Pirates' walk-off-caliber 3-2 win over Arizona further muddied the NL wild card picture.

  • Francisco Lindor [3-5, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 26] powered the Mets' 14-3 rout of Atlanta, with Marcus Semien [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 31] also going deep as New York gained a game in the NL East. (NYM)
  • Miami edged Philadelphia 8-7 in the day's second-largest WPA swing, gaining another game on the Braves. (BRAVES)
  • Pittsburgh beat Arizona 3-2 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA, with Merrill Kelly [5.2 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 4.87 ERA, PAR 9] turning in a strong no-run outing in the loss. (AZ)
  • Alex Bregman [4-5, 1 HR | RC 50] and Nico Hoerner [4-5, 1 HR | RC 46] each went 4-for-5 with a homer as the Cubs beat St. Louis 7-3 to gain a game in the NL Central. (CHC)
  • Cristian Javier [5 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 7.25 ERA, PAR -1] led all pitchers in PAR with 5 scoreless innings as Houston beat the Angels 6-4. (HOU)
  • Kumar Rocker [6.2 IP, 2 ER, 7 K | 4.05 ERA, PAR 22] and Joc Pederson [2-4, 2 HR | RC 49] (2 HR) fueled Texas past Seattle 7-3, dropping the Mariners further back in the AL West. (TEX)
  • Baltimore, Boston, Toronto, and New York all won, each gaining half a game on AL East-leading Tampa Bay.
  • Cleveland at Cincinnati was postponed.

The AL West race tightened as both the Angels and Mariners gained a game on the division-leading Rangers, while in the NL wild card picture, the Mets, Nationals, Pirates, and Reds all picked up ground. The day's most dramatic finish came in Baltimore, where the Braves edged the Orioles in a game with a 5.13 WPA swing.

  • Drew Rasmussen [7 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 3.08 ERA, PAR 36] led the Rays past the Guardians 1-0, dropping Cleveland further back in the AL Central. (TB)
  • The Braves beat the Orioles 3-2 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing. (BRAVES)
  • CJ Abrams [3-5, 2 HR | RC 81] and James Wood [2-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 90] each homered twice as the Nationals outslugged the Diamondbacks 10-7. (WSH)
  • The Pirates edged the Cubs 8-7, costing Chicago a game in the NL Central. (CUBS)
  • The Mets routed the Dodgers 8-3, gaining ground in the NL wild card race. (DODGERS)
  • The Angels and Mariners both won, each gaining a game on the AL West-leading Rangers. (MARINERS) (ANGELS)
  • Munetaka Murakami [3-5, 2 HR | RC 50] hit two homers as the White Sox crushed the Astros 12-3, while Jeremy Peña [2-4, 2 HR | RC 43] also went deep twice for Houston. (CWS)
  • Jacob Misiorowski [5 IP, 1 ER, 12 K | 1.58 ERA, PAR 56] struck out 12 as the Brewers routed the Rockies 11-2. (MIL)

Dylan Cease [9 IP, 0 ER, 12 K | 2.47 ERA, PAR 45]'s complete game shutout headlined the day as Toronto blanked Boston 6-0, dropping the Red Sox further back in the AL East. Meanwhile, Washington's win over Arizona cut into Atlanta's NL East lead, and Kansas City's 3-2 victory over Detroit—the day's most dramatic game by WPA—tightened the AL Central behind the White Sox.

  • Dylan Cease tossed a complete game shutout as the Blue Jays beat the Red Sox 6-0 at Fenway. (TOR)
  • The Royals edged the Tigers 3-2 in the day's most dramatic finish, gaining ground in the AL Central. (ROYALS)
  • CJ Abrams [3-4, 1 HR | RC 77] homered as the Nationals beat the Diamondbacks 5-3, gaining a game on Atlanta in the NL East. (WSH)
  • Pete Crow-Armstrong [4-5, 1 HR | RC 82] went 4-for-5 with a homer in the Cubs' 11-0 rout of the Pirates. (CHC)
  • Rafael Devers [3-4, 1 HR | RC 62] and Jung Hoo Lee [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 53] each homered as the Giants routed the Angels 9-2. (SF)
  • Hunter Brown [7 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 3.45 ERA, PAR 11] threw seven shutout innings in Houston's 4-1 win over the White Sox, gaining in the AL wild card race. (HOU)
  • Andre Pallante [7 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 3.77 ERA, PAR 28] tossed seven scoreless as the Cardinals shut out the Reds 7-0. (STL)
  • The Dodgers held off the Mets 4-3, while the Yankees beat the Phillies 3-1 and the Rays blanked the Guardians 3-0. (YANKEES) (GUARDIANS) (DODGERS)
